docs.title: lifi-py
docs.text:
A typed Python client for the LI.FI API — the bridge + DEX aggregator for any-to-any cross-chain swaps and bridges across 74 chains.

The killer feature: get_quote() returns a ready-to-sign transactionRequest directly — one call, no separate assemble step.

  • Sync (LifiClient) and async (AsyncLifiClient) clients on top of httpx.
  • All responses parsed into pydantic v2 models with full type hints (py.typed).
  • Built-in rate-limit awareness: reads the ratelimit-* headers, throttles proactively, and retries 429s with backoff.
  • Optional web3.py integration for signing/sending the returned transaction.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install lifi-py
# with web3 signing helpers:
pip install 'lifi-py[exec]'

docs.title: Quickstart — cross-chain quote with a ready-to-sign tx (keyless, <5 lines)
docs.text:
from lifi_py import LifiClient

quote = LifiClient().get_quote(
    from_chain=42161, to_chain=8453,                                  # Arbitrum -> Base
    from_token="0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831",          # USDC (Arbitrum)
    to_token="0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913",            # USDC (Base)
    from_amount="1000000", from_address="0x47E2D28169738039755586743E2dfCF3bd643f86",
)
print(quote.estimate.to_amount, quote.transaction_request.to)  # ~995000, 0x1231DEB6...

quote.transaction_request is an EVM transaction ready to sign and broadcast.

docs.title: Signing & sending (optional, [exec] extra)
docs.text:
tx = quote.transaction_request.as_web3_tx()   # hex fields decoded to ints, web3-shaped
signed = account.sign_transaction({**tx, "nonce": w3.eth.get_transaction_count(account.address)})
tx_hash = w3.eth.send_raw_transaction(signed.raw_transaction)

docs.title: Tracking a bridge to completion
docs.text:
client = LifiClient()
status = client.poll_status(tx_hash="0x...", bridge=quote.tool)  # polls until DONE/FAILED
print(status.status, status.is_done)

get_status() does a single check; poll_status() polls with exponential backoff until the transfer reaches a terminal state (or raises TimeoutError).

docs.title: Async
docs.text:
import asyncio
from lifi_py import AsyncLifiClient

async def main():
    async with AsyncLifiClient() as client:
        quote = await client.get_quote(...)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Authentication & rate limits
docs.text:
An API key is optional — every endpoint above works keyless. A key only raises your rate limits:

client = LifiClient(api_key="your-key")                 # sent as `x-lifi-api-key`
client = LifiClient(api_key="k", api_key_header="x-custom-key")  # configurable header
client = LifiClient(base_url="https://staging.li.quest/v1")      # configurable base URL

The client reads the API's ratelimit-limit / ratelimit-remaining / ratelimit-reset response headers (exposed via client.rate_limit). When the quota is exhausted it pauses before the next request; on a 429 it retries with backoff respecting the reset window, raising LifiRateLimitError once retries are exhausted.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Argument Default Description api_key None Optional; raises rate limits. base_url https://li.quest/v1 API base URL. api_key_header x-lifi-api-key Header name for the key. timeout 30.0 Per-request timeout (seconds). max_retries 3 Max 429 retries before raising. http_client None Inject your own httpx.Client / AsyncClient.

docs.title: AsyncLifiClient
docs.text:
Asynchronous client for the LI.FI API.

A coroutine-based mirror of :class:LifiClient with identical endpoints, parameters and return types. Use it as an async context manager so the underlying HTTP connections are closed on exit.

The API key is optional (it only raises rate limits); all endpoints work keyless. The client tracks the ratelimit-* response headers, pauses proactively when the quota is exhausted, and retries 429s with backoff.

Example

import asyncio async def main(): ... async with AsyncLifiClient() as client: ... return await client.get_chains() chains = asyncio.run(main()) # doctest: +SKIP

docs.title: get_quote(*, from_chain, to_chain, from_token, to_token, from_amount, from_address, to_address=None, slippage=None, order=None, integrator=None)
docs.text:
Get the best single-step quote with a ready-to-sign transaction.

This is the headline call: the returned :class:~lifi_py.Quote carries a :attr:~lifi_py.Quote.transaction_request you can sign and broadcast directly — no separate assembly step.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default from_chain ChainRef

Source chain id (or LI.FI chain key).

required to_chain ChainRef

Destination chain id (or LI.FI chain key).

required from_token str

Source token address (zero address for native).

required to_token str

Destination token address.

required from_amount str

Amount to send, as an integer string in the source token's smallest unit (e.g. "1000000" for 1 USDC).

required from_address str

Wallet sending the funds.

required to_address Optional[str]

Recipient on the destination chain. Defaults to from_address when omitted.

None slippage Optional[float]

Allowed slippage as a fraction, e.g. 0.005 for 0.5%.

None order Optional[str]

Routing preference, e.g. "CHEAPEST" or "FASTEST".

None integrator Optional[str]

Integrator string attributed to the request.

None

Returns:

Type Description Quote

The best route, including a ready-to-sign transaction_request.

Raises:

Type Description LifiAPIError

The API rejected the request (e.g. unsupported route).

LifiRateLimitError

Rate limited after exhausting retries.

Example

client = LifiClient() quote = client.get_quote( ... from_chain=42161, to_chain=8453, # Arbitrum -> Base ... from_token="0xaf88d065e77c8cC2239327C5EDb3A432268e5831", # USDC ... to_token="0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913", # USDC ... from_amount="1000000", # 1 USDC ... from_address="0x47E2D28169738039755586743E2dfCF3bd643f86", ... ) quote.estimate.to_amount # doctest: +SKIP '995000' quote.transaction_request.to # doctest: +SKIP '0x1231DEB6f5749EF6cE6943a275A1D3E7486F4EaE'

docs.text:
Poll /status with exponential backoff until DONE or FAILED.

Repeatedly calls :meth:get_status, sleeping between attempts with the delay doubling from interval up to max_interval, until the transfer reaches a terminal state.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default tx_hash str

The source-chain transaction hash to track.

required bridge Optional[str]

The bridge/tool key used (recommended; speeds up lookups).

None from_chain Optional[ChainRef]

Source chain id, to disambiguate the lookup.

None to_chain Optional[ChainRef]

Destination chain id, to disambiguate the lookup.

None interval float

Initial delay between polls, in seconds.

5.0 timeout float

Maximum total time to wait, in seconds.

300.0 max_interval float

Cap on the (exponentially growing) poll delay.

30.0

Returns:

Type Description Status

The terminal :class:~lifi_py.Status (DONE or FAILED).

Raises:

Type Description TimeoutError

No terminal state was reached within timeout.

LifiAPIError

A status request failed.

LifiRateLimitError

Rate limited after exhausting retries.

Example

client = LifiClient() final = client.poll_status(tx_hash="0x...", bridge="across") # doctest: +SKIP final.is_done # doctest: +SKIP True

docs.title: LifiError
docs.text:
Bases: Exception

Base class for all errors raised by this library.

Catch this to handle any lifi-py-originated failure regardless of kind. Note that low-level transport failures (timeouts, connection errors) propagate as the underlying :class:httpx.HTTPError subclasses, not as LifiError.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Bases: _Model

Result of GET /status while tracking a cross-chain transfer.

:attr:status is one of NOT_FOUND, PENDING, DONE or FAILED (INVALID may also appear). Use :attr:is_done, :attr:is_failed and :attr:is_terminal instead of comparing strings.

docs.title: is_done property
docs.text: True when the transfer completed successfully (status == "DONE").

docs.title: is_failed property
docs.text: True when the transfer failed (status is FAILED or INVALID).

docs.title: is_terminal property
docs.text: True once the transfer reached a final state and won't change.

docs.title: Step
docs.text:

A simple transfer has a single step; complex routes chain several. After fetching calldata (POST /advanced/stepTransaction) the step carries a populated :attr:transaction_request.

docs.text:
Return a dict shaped for web3.eth.send_transaction / signing.

Hex-encoded numeric fields (value, gasLimit, gasPrice) are decoded to int and gasLimit is renamed to gas; to/data are passed through unchanged. Only fields that are set are included, so you can merge in your own nonce/from before signing.

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, Any]

A mapping ready to pass to web3.py signing/sending APIs.

Example

tx = quote.transaction_request.as_web3_tx() tx["nonce"] = w3.eth.get_transaction_count(account.address) signed = account.sign_transaction(tx) w3.eth.send_raw_transaction(signed.raw_transaction)
